# Anti-Patterns (D3): construction moves that produce limited value

Derived from the corpus records flagged `negative_case` plus corroborating
evidence in non-flagged records. Each entry states the reusable
"don't replicate" rule. Citations are corpus IDs (see `data/corpus/papers.json`).

## AP-1 — Template QA that answers itself
**What gets built:** VQA datasets generated by slot-filling templates over
label maps, with small vocabularies and skewed answer distributions.
**Why value is limited:** models learn the language prior, not the imagery —
visual-blind models score competitively, so the nominal "VQA capability" is
partly illusory; biases are worse than in natural-image VQA
([2311.16782](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.16782)).
**Rule:** never claim a capability from template-QA accuracy alone; report
bias-controlled metrics (visual-blind baselines, adversarial visual input) for
any deterministically generated QA supervision.

## AP-2 — Fluency mistaken for capability
**What gets built:** benchmarks/models where open-ended description looks
impressive, so spatially grounded competence is assumed.
**Why value is limited:** state-of-the-art VLMs caption EO scenes well but fail
at localization and counting ([2401.17600](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.17600));
the best model on a purpose-built geospatial benchmark scores 41.7% on MCQs,
about double random ([2411.19325](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.19325)).
**Rule:** every claimed capability needs a task-grounded metric that fluency
cannot satisfy (counts, coordinates, per-instance decisions), not caption
quality scores.

## AP-3 — Assuming zero-shot transfer into expert domains
**What gets built:** applications that drop an off-the-shelf VLM into a
specialist recognition task with class-name prompts.
**Why value is limited:** zero-shot VLMs substantially underperform a plain
supervised baseline across 27 agricultural tasks, with open-ended accuracy
often under 25% ([2512.15977](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.15977)); zero-shot
RemoteCLIP hits 4.9% top-1 on roof materials before domain fine-tuning lifts
it to 47.7% ([2505.19358](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.19358)).
**Rule:** treat zero-shot as a lower bound to report, not a deployment plan;
expert-domain pairings must budget for domain supervision (which is exactly
what the metapatterns are for).

## AP-4 — The imagery-to-statistics leap
**What gets built:** supervision that pairs imagery directly with
area-aggregated socioeconomic or outcome statistics and expects the model to
"see" them.
**Why value is limited:** even a 17-city, 6-domain benchmark finds LVLMs
unreliable at predicting urban socioeconomic indicators from imagery
([2506.00530](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.00530)); the semantic relationship is
correlational, not observational — the language asserts things the pixels
underdetermine.
**Rule:** pair language with what the geodata actually evidences; when the
target is an aggregate statistic, make the mediating observable explicit
(e.g., building attributes → heat demand via a stated model,
[2602.20066](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20066)) or don't build the pairing.

## AP-5 — LLM-synthesized supervision without hallucination control
**What gets built:** large caption/instruction corpora generated by an LLM/VLM
from thin seeds, with no measurement of fabricated content.
**Why value is limited:** LLM captions are prone to generic text and
hallucination that then trains the downstream model; grounding in external
sources and measuring hallucination is required for the data to help
([2501.14905](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14905)); un-grounded generations show
hallucination, repetition, and incoherence until knowledge-graph vocabulary is
injected ([2509.21609](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.21609)).
**Rule:** any `llm-synthesis` pipeline must ship a measured hallucination/QC
rate against an authoritative source, or the dataset is not evidence of a
capability.

## AP-6 — Stopping at the benchmark
**What gets built:** dataset + fine-tuned model + leaderboard, with the
operational user never named.
**Why value is limited:** in this corpus 30/59 works sit at
`benchmark-research` maturity and only 5 reach decision-support prototype or
beyond (counts from `analysis/corpus_stats.py`); capability without a named
workflow rarely translates into scientific or operational use — all 16 records
with `use_enabled: none identified` sit at benchmark-research maturity, and no
corpus record reaches operational-prototype or deployed.
**Rule:** a new geodata-language pairing should name, at spec time, the
workflow and decision its capability serves (the Spec Card makes this field
mandatory); "the community can build on it" is not an application.
